items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1983-05-28
items.q: The interviewee does not speak about Louis Armstrong directly; the interviewer mentions Louis Armstrong in the context of a story about D Pierce and Buddy Petit.

ctx.x: well I think back then we were fascinated and we thought tradition was was something that had some age and status of its own when actually I think we both learned in time that it might not mean anything at all and often didn't yeah well

people would say that's a traditional Louis Armstrong they can I can remember talking to the D Pierce at Lutton's about something and he said something he picked up from Buddy Petit an ending that he played that people associate with Louis the sort of thing Louis played in Cornette Chop Suey anyway uh Frank Murray was down there seems to me it was a non-union band with Octave Coleman on drums and John Casimir on clarinet and maybe John got in trouble I don't kind of mind mentioning that to somebody I don't know
hmm he belonged in the union

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: Did you consider them part of the same tradition or? Yeah, I did.

ctx.x: And I was very impressed by them. I never did hear as much of them as I wanted to.

Uh-huh. Let's see. Now, uh, when you go out and buy 78s or LPs, you mentioned in particular liking Joe H. Lewis's. Yeah. Did you consider that different from, say, King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band or Louis Armstrong and his Hot Five? Did you consider them part of the same tradition or?
Yeah, I did. I wasn't sure what you meant by different. No, as far as I was concerned.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: talk about King Oliver and Louis Armstrong, all the time we're walking around

ctx.x: Yeah. There was that. Of course you knew Johnny better than I did anyway.

Well, you were busy with medical school. Yeah. And I was either hanging around, looking for a job, or working in the shop. Yeah. Do you remember something that amazed me? When he'd be feeling good, we'd take a walk over to Rampart Street, and talk about King Oliver and Louis Armstrong, all the time we're walking around, looking at the sights. This is South Rampart Street. Yeah. Smelling the food and stuff. And then we'd get in a bad mood. All he wanted to talk about was pigs. And we'd have a, I have a laugh. And…
And Johnny would say, the trouble with you people is you don't understand Vicks.
